records.bodyText:
Another of our Press Releases picked up by our friends at Scottish Farmer! 
Twelve Necessary Wayleave hearings have been postponed by the DPEA.
As John Campbell, our NOTKUP Project Manager says, “This is not a minor administrative adjustment. It is a direct consequence of the strength of the objectors’ case and the seriousness of the agricultural evidence that has been put before the Reporters.
“The message from this decision is unmistakable - the impacts on farming businesses are real, they are relevant and they must be properly considered before any compulsory rights are imposed over land.”
And the Reporters have listened!

records.title: No Pylons Lincolnshire
records.bodyText:
A week ago we submitted a second set of questions relating to WMEL - National Grid have decided to treat them as Freedom of Information Request despite the questions being relevant to the consultation. 
Here is the latest response:
Dear Cat
Thank you for your email. 
The EIR request will be handled through the appropriate Environmental Information Regulations process, and we'll provide a response once that process has been completed. As mentioned in our previous reply, we will work to the statutory time frame of 20 days.  
As many of the questions you raised are interdependent, the best way for us to provide complete and clear answers is in a single written response. For that reason, we will not be responding to each question separately as we go. 
We will be providing a direct response to you, but we will not publish that information on our project website. We are committed to making relevant project information available through our consultation materials and reporting, while managing individual correspondence
 through appropriate channels.  
We are aware that the EIR response deadline falls within four days of the close of consultation, however you and other members of the public are more than welcome to provide feedback ahead of receiving the EIR response, and after. All feedback submitted to
 the project in advance of the close of consultation will be considered. 
We will not be extending the consultation period. We believe the consultation period strikes an appropriate balance between providing meaningful opportunities for participation and maintaining the project's overall programme.  
Kind regards
Community Relations Team  
Weston Marsh to East Leicestershire

records.bodyText:
SCOTLAND’S landscape is being altered faster than at any other time in the race to Net Zero, a leading ecologist has warned.
Dr James Fenton helped to draft key safeguards designed to protect National Scenic Areas (NSAs), while at Scottish Government agency NatureScot.
But the expert fears there is now a ‘fundamental problem’ with the protections, claiming SNP ministers are pushing through large-scale afforestation schemes with ‘insufficient oversight’ – leading to the erosion of ‘precious’ moorlands ‘faster now than at any time in the past’.

records.bodyText:
Join us for a webinar at lunchtime Monday 19th October called 'who pays for Big Tech'
We will explore the findings of a recent report on the social, economic, and environmental costs of data centres in Ireland, with researchers from University College Dublin and Maynooth University.
Patrick Brodie and Patrick Bresnihan will cover their research on how claims about the economic benefits of data centres to Ireland are exaggerated, the costs of data centre development are socialised through existing industrial policy, and the current policy contradictory to long-term sustainability goals.
Link in bio
More about the speakers
Patrick Brodie is a Lecturer/Assistant Professor and Ad Astra Fellow in the School of Information and Communication Studies at University College Dublin. His research focuses on the environmental politics of digital infrastructures, and specifically the relations and entanglements of internet and other communications technologies with energy systems, global supply chains, and extractivism.
Patrick Bresnihan is an Associate Professor in the Department of Geography at Maynooth University. His work examines the contested politics of climate, land, and infrastructure in Ireland, and how these speak to broader questions of postcolonial development, dependency and the green transition.

Noise: Important webinar to watch
We often reference noise on this page, especially the health hazards of low frequency sound waves, and lots of you ask questions about it or send videos of noise we often can't authenticate but wish we could. This YouTube link is to a webinar organised by the UK Noise Association, and has two very well qualified speakers who talk about both the health impacts and technical aspects of noise. Together with their slides, it's hugely instructive. If you can find an hour sometime to watch it, please stick with it - it has the usual webinar hiccups, but well worth watching to the end.

records.bodyText:
Notes from Community Council special Hyperscale Data Centre meeting.
I attended last nights meeting and left early as the meeting was not focused on the Hyperscale Data Centre.
The meeting was held by BenMorse the chair of the CC and the sub group of the community council specifically created to work on the Hyperscale data centre. Ther were no introductions only Ben Morse the chair speaking, no representatives from SDCL or ELC. The meeting was disapppointing and focused on what we already know about the power station site. It was a repeat of the last two meetings when they discussed the site. Anyone attending knows the history and whats on the site and is attending because they want to put a stop to the Hyperscale Data Centre after all thats what the meeting was advertised as.
I learnt that ELC, Councillors Gilbert and another along with representation from each development site, whether in person or via email met with the chairs of Prestonpans and Cockenzie and Port Seton Community Councils. These meetings have been set up to improve communication but no minutes were released only a mention of funding available from Inch Cape, the promise of jobs and that Seagreen have delayed building work.
This feedback was not helpful and not what I was led to believe these meetings were for.
Ben Morse chair of Cockenzie & Port Seton CC reminded the group that there were no plans yet for the data centre, which we are well aware of. He did not seem to appreciate that now is the time to email councillors as to the reasons why we dont want a Hyperscale data centre and that we have to try and stop the SDCL agreement being signed.
There was also no mention of the CC supporting the land asset transfer by the 360 project and no mention of the cc looking into the fact that the site was bought with public money and that deals were done behind closed doors.
There was also no mention that we need to be prepared for when the plans are released.
He stated a new ELC development plan was in the pipeline.
He also mentioned the gas leak but played it down. I then asked him if the community council had reported our health and Safety concerns to SEPA and the Health and Safety Executive re the accumulation of the fire, the gas leak, the contaminated dust, the asbestos, the working outwith hours, the monitoring of air quality etc. He said yes but no one had replied to their emails.
I explained ELCs complaints procedure to him and how we could following the correct procedures request a public enquiry.
I asked for the CC to be more active in supporting the community as we have no faith in ELCs health and Safety at the power station site see my previous letter to the cc which they have not replied to.
I feel that our concerns over H&S are what should have been discussed at the site meeting mentioned previously.
I then left as it was very clear that the meeting was going nowhere but over old ground.
Ive been informed the meeting finally got onto the data centre at 9pm. Im awaiting an update from anyone who was there.
If anyone is interested please join our community council they are short of members and definitely require more local people who are passionate about stopping the data centre.

records.title: RE-Think Wales
records.bodyText:
Planning Aid Wales (‘We support meaningful community engagement in planning in Wales’) are offering a series of online seminars on infrastructure planning. The first, Understanding Planning Infrastructure for Communities, provided an overview of the planning system, and how to engage in the new Significant Infrastructure Projects (SIP) process. For campaigners already broadly familiar with the planning system, there was nothing new, as such, but one or two things did fall into place for me.
The second 2 hour session, on 11 November, is on Responding to Infrastructure Planning Applications, and will explore “how communities can respond confidently to SIPs, with a particular focus on preparing evidence-based representations that can make a meaningful contribution to the examination process.” Cost is £20. https://planningaidwales.org.uk/.../planning-your-places-7/
Then on 11 November there’s a free Infrastructure Planning: Community Perspectives Roundtable. This will be “A facilitated, exploratory session to surface the questions and issues communities have about the new national infrastructure planning process in Wales…Bring your questions, share examples from your own area and hear from others facing similar opportunities and challenges. The discussion will explore how communities are engaging with the new process, what is working well, and where further support may be needed.” https://planningaidwales.org.uk/.../planning-your-places-9/
The final session, on 20 January 2027, is on Community Engagement in Infrastructure Planning Applications, and will explore “how communities can engage positively and effectively throughout the infrastructure planning process, from the earliest stages of project development through to decision-making.”
I know, positive engagement with Bute Energy/Green GEN and their ilk is an oxymoron.
The first session was run by the Planning Aid Wales Chief Executive, who proved open to challenge and willing to learn from participants’ experiences. On Monday he’s running a new session on Planning & Artificial Intelligence - Smarter Tools, Stronger Communities (cost £40). https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/.../planning-artificial...
https://www.facebook.com/planningaidwales
